allocations.description: Allocate one timer of TIM1, TIM2, TIM8, TIM12 or TIM15 and a pad one of its channels is routed to, for PWM, output compare or input capture written by the application. Allocation only: no code is generated and the timer is not shared.
allocations.guidance: Allocation only; no component is generated. resource_bindings gives the timer's hal_instance and clock_enable_api, the pad's port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api, and under routes the selected signal with its alternate_symbol and channel_symbol. The application enables the TIM module if no other selected card does (USE_HAL_TIM_MODULE in generated/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_conf.h and stm32c5xx_drivers/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_tim.c in CMakeLists.txt), enables both clocks, initializes the pad with mode HAL_GPIO_MODE_ALTERNATE and the route's alternate_symbol, and drives the channel through the SDK TIM API in stm32c5xx_hal_tim.h starting from HAL_TIM_Init with the allocated hal_instance. Period, duty, polarity, compare or capture mode, complementary outputs, dead time and break are application decisions. One counter serves all channels, so the allocation takes the whole timer. No timing, electrical or errata qualification.

allocations.description: Allocate a pad routed to an external input of ADC1 for analog conversion written by the application. Allocation only: no code is generated; the converter is shared, one allocation per offered input. Not to be combined with analog_reading on the same converter. Pads that need the SBS pin remap are not offered.
allocations.guidance: Allocation only; no component is generated. resource_bindings gives the converter's hal_instance and clock_enable_api, the pad's port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api, and under routes the selected signal with its channel_symbol. The application enables the ADC module (USE_HAL_ADC_MODULE in generated/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_conf.h and stm32c5xx_drivers/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_adc.c in CMakeLists.txt), enables both clocks, initializes the pad with mode HAL_GPIO_MODE_ANALOG, and configures and reads the converter through the SDK ADC API in stm32c5xx_hal_adc.h starting from HAL_ADC_Init with the allocated hal_instance. The converter is one shared unit: sequencing of several inputs, sampling time, calibration, reference voltage and accuracy are application decisions. Internal channels, injected and differential conversion are not covered. Only the pad each input uses without the SBS pin remap is offered: PC4, PC5, PB0 and PB1 need the SBS pin remap and are excluded, so no remap is required. Not together with analog_reading on the same converter: its generated units own the converter's configuration. The two hold the converter in different ownership modes, so a request with both on one converter is refused. When the engine has confirmed that ownership is what stands in the way, the refusal says so and names the converter under ownership_conflicts. No electrical or errata qualification.

allocations.description: One edge-aligned PWM output on a covered channel timer and a pad one of its channels is routed to. The frequency is one of the exact divisions of the pinned 144MHz timer clock; duty is set at run time in thousandths of the period. Generated component with init, start, set duty and stop. The whole timer belongs to the output.
allocations.guidance: Generated component owns the timer handle, the time base, one compare unit in PWM mode 1 with preload, the channel and the pad. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the timer, the channel or the pad again. Supports only the listed frequencies at the captured 144MHz kernel clock: each has an exact prescaler and period, the period is at least 1000 counts and full duty fits a 16-bit compare register. Duty is thousandths of the period rounded down to a whole count; the duty in force from a period boundary on is the last one written before it. The first period after a start can be shorter at the pad; that it is not longer follows from the order of the calls and is not measured. start and stop belong to one thread; set duty may also run in an interrupt. Active high, counting up, internal clock; no dithering, complementary output, dead time, break input, one-pulse or any other channel of the timer. On a timer with a break function the SDK sets the main output enable when the channel starts. The level of the pad while stopped is not established. Init verifies the clock and register factors; dynamic clock changes are outside the contract. Build is not a measurement of frequency, duty or edge quality.

cites.statement: BKPT exact PWM frequency domain derived from the pinned 144MHz profile: prescaler and period for each choice, period between 999 and 65534. Arithmetic on the nominal clock, not measured timing.

RM0522 page 989, PWM mode 1 counting up: the reference signal is high while the counter is below the compare register, held at 1 when the compare value is above the auto-reload value and held at 0 when it is zero. Text extraction.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; private timer handle, time base, compare unit, channel and pad. No manual timer, channel or GPIO setup.
interface.start: {{unit}}_start(duty_permille), 0..1000: checked HAL_OK restarts the counter and then enables the nominal {{frequency_hz}}Hz output, so the first period at the pad can be shorter than a full one; later periods are whole by the timer's own counting, which is not measured. One thread only, never from an interrupt; fails while running.
interface.set_duty: {{unit}}_set_duty(duty_permille), 0..1000, rounded down to a whole count of the {{period}}+1 count period: checked HAL_OK; the duty in force from a period boundary on is the last one written before it. Fails unless running. Owning thread or an interrupt; an interrupt that preempts start or stop gets a failure until start has finished and from the moment stop begins.
interface.stop: {{unit}}_stop(): checked HAL_OK stops the output, then the counter; idempotent when stopped. One thread only, never from an interrupt.
interface.scope: Exact factors and run-time clock/register checks for the pinned 144MHz profile. Active high, edge aligned. No clock changes, complementary outputs, dead time, break inputs, other channels, DMA or measured timing. The pad level while stopped is not established.

allocations.description: Read one analog input of a covered converter on request: a generated unit per input with init and a blocking read that returns the 12-bit count, the pad voltage as a fraction of VREF+. The units share the converter and own its configuration, so every offered input may have one unit, and no analog input allocation may be used on the same converter beside them. Pads that need the SBS pin remap are not offered.
allocations.guidance: Generated component. The first unit on a converter sets the ADC and DAC kernel clock to HCLK divided by 8 (18MHz in the captured 144MHz profile) before it enables the converter's bus clock, reads the clock configuration back, sets 12-bit resolution, software trigger and one conversion per request, activates the converter and runs its offset calibration; every unit on that converter shares the one handle, and each unit switches its own pad to analog mode. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the converter, its clock or the pad again. The units own the converter: do not combine them with an analog_input_pin allocation on the same converter. The two hold the converter in different ownership modes, so a request that makes that combination is refused. When the engine has confirmed that ownership is what stands in the way, the refusal says so and names the converter under ownership_conflicts. read converts once with the SDK's longest sampling time and returns counts 0..4095, right aligned: a fraction of VREF+, not volts, because the reference is not measured. Before each conversion the unit checks on the converter itself that it is enabled, idle and holds this input; it selects its input again when another is held, which stops, switches, starts and calibrates the converter, and it reports HAL_ERROR for good when the converter was stopped or is converting behind it. Every wait is the SDK's and counts HAL ticks, which must be advancing; a wait gives up when the ticks exceed its limit, so up to one tick after it. The conversion has a limit of 2ms, and when it does not finish the unit stops it, where the SDK waits with a limit of 2ms again, before it returns HAL_TIMEOUT: up to about 6ms of ticks. A switch adds the SDK's limits of 2ms to disable, 2ms to enable and 228ms for the calibration: at most about a quarter of a second of ticks. These count ticks and not time for the caller: a delayed thread takes longer by its delay. One thread only, never from an interrupt. The same kernel clock feeds the DAC. No internal channels, injected or differential conversion, triggers, interrupts, DMA, oversampling or analog watchdog. PC4, PC5, PB0 and PB1 need the SBS pin remap and are excluded. Accuracy, source impedance and noise are not qualified; build is not a measurement.

cites.statement: DS15135 page 76, ADC characteristics: the ADC clock frequency fADC is 8 to 36 MHz for a VDDA of 2.7 to 3.6 V. Text extraction of a table; the row is quoted, the table layout is not visually validated.
SDK build adds hal_adc.c only under its HAL ADC component selection; the captured build selects no such component, so the file is added through the root extension point.
DS15135 page 77, ADC characteristics: sampling time tS from 2.5 to 288.5 cycles of the ADC clock. Text extraction of a table row; the SDK names its longest setting 289 cycles.
SDK ADC deactivation, used by HAL_ADC_Stop: outside calibration it disables the internal regulator and enters deep power-down, which is why a unit calibrates again after it switches its input.
SDK ADC calibration: it starts the self-calibration and waits for its end against ADC_CALIBRATION_TIMEOUT_MS, counted with HAL_GetTick, and reports an error when the limit passes.

SDK ADC polled conversion: it waits for the end-of-conversion flag and returns HAL_TIMEOUT when the HAL ticks passed since the call are greater than the limit it was given, so not before one tick more than the limit.

SDK ADC stop of a regular conversion: after the stop request it waits until no conversion is ongoing and gives up when the HAL ticks passed are greater than ADC_CONV_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS. The unit calls it after a conversion that timed out.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; the converter, its kernel clock, calibration and the pad {{pad_name}} are set up. No manual ADC, clock or GPIO setup.
interface.read: {{unit}}_read(&counts): checked HAL_OK converts this input once and writes counts 0..4095, the pad voltage as a fraction of VREF+ in steps of 1/4096. Not volts: the reference is not measured. Blocking. The waits count HAL ticks, which must be advancing, and each ends up to one tick after its limit. When the converter holds this input: a limit of 2ms for the conversion and, when it does not finish, 2ms again to stop it before HAL_TIMEOUT, up to about 6ms of ticks. When it has to switch from another input: in addition the SDK's limits to disable and to enable the converter and 228ms for the calibration, at most about a quarter of a second of ticks. A delayed thread takes longer by its delay. One thread only, never from an interrupt, never while another unit of the same converter reads.
interface.scope: 12-bit, software trigger, the SDK's longest sampling time, 18MHz converter clock set before the bus clock and checked at init for the pinned 144MHz profile. The units own the converter: no analog_input_pin allocation and no application ADC calls on it. A converter found stopped or converting behind the unit is a permanent HAL_ERROR. No internal channels, triggers, interrupts, DMA, oversampling or measured accuracy.

allocations.description: Measure the period and high time of a digital signal on a pad one channel of a covered timer is routed to: a generated unit with init and a blocking, polled measurement in microseconds with a time limit counted on the timer. The whole timer belongs to the measurement.
allocations.guidance: Generated component owns the timer handle, a 1MHz time base over a 16-bit period, capture of both edges on the allocated channel's own pin, the compare flag of the other of the timer's first two channels as a half-turn mark (that channel drives no pad), and the pad as an input with the selected pull. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the timer, a channel or the pad again. measure waits for a rising edge, the falling edge after it and the next rising edge and returns period and high time in whole microseconds of the timer clock. The time limit, 1..60000 ms, is counted on the same clock from the start of the counter: an edge at or after the limit is not used, and HAL_TIMEOUT means that the three edges did not all occur before it. The unit polls. In each pass it reads the count and the status, acknowledges the marks it saw and reads the marks again, as one step with interrupts masked for those three or four register accesses, and it ends the measurement with HAL_ERROR when both marks are set at once, when a mark is set behind an acknowledgement, on the overcapture flag, or when a further edge arrives while one is read. Provided that nothing else writes the timer and that the timer and the pad behave as the reference manual describes, HAL_OK comes with the true period and high time, wherever and for however long the calling thread was delayed, and a delay the unit cannot resolve ends in HAL_ERROR and not in a value. A measurement completes without that error when the thread is not delayed for 32ms or longer between two passes and each edge is read before the next one arrives; a delay of 65.536ms or more from one pass to the next sets both marks. The basis is the reasoning in the unit's source and a host model that runs the unit's template against a simulated timer (stm32c5/tests/input_capture_model.py); on a board only delays between two passes were provoked. A delayed thread returns later by its delay, also past the limit. One thread only, never from an interrupt. No input filter, prescaled capture, interrupt or DMA capture or XOR input. Init verifies the clock and register factors for the pinned 144MHz profile; times are counts of the nominal clock, not measured against a reference.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; private timer handle, 1MHz time base, capture of both edges, a half-turn mark on another channel's flag, interrupts masked for three or four register accesses in each pass of a measurement, and the pad {{pad_name}} as an input with pull {{pull}}. No manual timer, channel or GPIO setup.
interface.measure: {{unit}}_measure(timeout_ms, &period_us, &high_us), timeout 1..60000 counted on the timer from the start of its counter: checked HAL_OK waited for the first rising edge the channel captured, the falling edge after it and the next rising edge, all before the limit, and wrote period and high time in microseconds. HAL_TIMEOUT when the three edges did not all occur before the limit. HAL_ERROR when the unit could not follow the counter or the edges: a delay of the calling thread that it cannot resolve (possible from 32ms between two passes, both marks set from 65.536ms), or an edge that arrived before the previous one was read. Blocking; one thread only, never from an interrupt.
interface.scope: Polled capture with a microsecond count for the pinned 144MHz profile, checked at init and before each measurement. What HAL_OK and HAL_TIMEOUT mean holds provided that nothing else writes the timer and that timer and pad behave as the reference manual describes; it was checked on a host model of the timer, and on a board for delays between two passes only. No stated minimum pulse width, input filter, interrupt or DMA capture or measured accuracy. Outputs are written only with HAL_OK.

instance_capabilities.description: Periodic update interrupt on a timer the timer channel allocation covers, with the generated component, exact rate choices and rules of periodic_interrupt on TIM6 and TIM7, unchanged. It takes the whole timer and its update vector and uses no channel or pad; use it when the basic timers are taken or more periodic interrupts are needed.
instance_capabilities.guidance: The reviewed periodic update component on a channel timer. Generated component owns persistent timer state, callback adapter, initialization, clock/factor verification, fresh-period start/stop and vector dispatch. Use returned interface; do not duplicate timer setup or weak callbacks. Supports only the complete declared set of exact nominal integer rates1..1000 at the captured144MHz kernel. PSC<=65534 and ARR1..65535; repetition0, upcounter/internal clock, no dithering. Init and start verify actual clock/register factors. Any dynamic clock changes are outside contract. Per-instance callback runs in IRQ context and must remain bounded; main/thread owns start/stop. Application chooses tick meaning. Build is not hardware rate/latency verification. The update vector is the timer's own update vector or, on a timer with one vector, its global vector; only the update event is enabled, and no channel of the timer is used.

instance_capabilities.description: CRC-32 (ISO 3309, zlib) of a buffer of bytes on the hardware CRC unit: a generated unit with init and a one-call computation. The whole CRC unit belongs to it.
instance_capabilities.guidance: Generated component owns the CRC handle and its configuration: polynomial 0x04C11DB7, initial value 0xFFFFFFFF, every input byte and the result bit-reversed; the unit inverts the result. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the CRC unit again. compute takes a buffer of 1 or more bytes, starts from the initial value on every call and returns the CRC-32 whose value for the ASCII characters 123456789 is 0xCBF43926. One thread only, never from an interrupt. No other polynomial or size, no accumulation across calls, no DMA. The check value is arithmetic for testing a build, not a measurement.

cites.statement: SDK build adds hal_crc.c only under its HAL CRC component selection; the captured build selects no such component, so the file is added through the root extension point.
SDK CRC data feed, used by HAL_CRC_Calculate: it writes the buffer to the data register in buffer order, whole words first and the remaining one to three bytes after them.

interface.setup: Already initialized after mx_system_init. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; private CRC handle and configuration. No manual CRC or clock setup.
interface.compute: {{unit}}_compute(data, bytes, &crc32), bytes 1 or more: checked HAL_OK writes the CRC-32 of the buffer, computed from the initial value. Nothing is carried between calls. One thread only, never from an interrupt.
interface.scope: CRC-32 of ISO 3309 and zlib only: 123456789 gives 0xCBF43926. No other polynomial, size or accumulation.

hal_status_t {{unit}}_init(void);
hal_status_t {{unit}}_compute(const void *data, uint32_t bytes, uint32_t *crc32);

instance_capabilities.description: Independent watchdog with a chosen reset time: a generated unit that prepares the watchdog, and start, refresh, the time actually set and a state for the application. Once started it resets the microcontroller unless refreshed in time and cannot be stopped; a start that fails may leave it running.
instance_capabilities.guidance: Generated component owns the watchdog handle. Generated init only prepares it: the application calls start when it is ready, and from then on must call refresh within the reset time or the microcontroller resets. The watchdog cannot be stopped or reconfigured before a reset, so start it only when the refresh path is in place. The reset time is the selected number of milliseconds at the nominal 32kHz of the low-speed internal oscillator; timeout_ms reports the time the driver set, and the oscillator's real frequency shifts it. While start runs, state reports 3 and refresh returns HAL_BUSY and writes nothing: a refresh writes the reload key, the reference manual states that any key but the access key write-protects the watchdog's registers again, and the SDK writes the access key and then the prescaler and the reload value, so a refresh from an interrupt inside start could leave the watchdog with other values than the unit reports. The SDK enables the watchdog before it waits for its registers, and those waits can fail: when start returns an error other than busy, state reports 2, the watchdog may be running with a reset time that is not known, timeout_ms reports 0xFFFFFFFF, refresh still restarts the count, start cannot be tried again, and a reset may follow. No window (a refresh is allowed at any time) and no early interrupt. refresh may be called from the owning thread or an interrupt, and is refused from an interrupt that arrives while start runs; start from the thread only. Behaviour while a debugger halts the core and in low-power modes, and the option bytes, are not covered. Build does not exercise the reset.

cites.statement: SDK build adds hal_iwdg.c only under its HAL IWDG component selection; the captured build selects no such component, so the file is added through the root extension point.

RM0522 page 1538, IWDG key register: writing 0xAAAA reloads the counter and write-protects the registers, 0x5555 enables write access to them, and any value different from 0x5555 write-protects them. Text extraction.

RM0522 page 1534, section 37.4.6: the prescaler, reload, early wake-up and window registers are write-protected until 0x0000 5555 is written to the key register. Text extraction; the sentence on other values is cut by a figure on these lines and is cited from the key register description.
SDK IWDG start: it enables the watchdog, enables write access and then writes the prescaler and the reload value, in this order and before its waits.

interface.setup: Prepared after mx_system_init, not running. Header bkpt_components/{{unit}}.h; private watchdog handle.
interface.start: {{unit}}_start(): checked HAL_OK starts the watchdog with a nominal reset time of {{timeout_ms}} ms; it cannot be stopped afterwards. HAL_BUSY when a start was already made. While it runs, state is 3 and refresh is refused. Any other result is a failed start after which the watchdog may be running with a reset time that is not known: state is 2 and a reset may follow. Thread only.
interface.refresh: {{unit}}_refresh(): checked HAL_OK restarts the count; call it more often than the reset time. Thread or interrupt. HAL_ERROR before any start; HAL_BUSY, with nothing written, while start is running; after a failed start the count is restarted all the same.
interface.timeout: {{unit}}_timeout_ms(): the reset time the driver set, in milliseconds of the nominal oscillator; 0 before start; 0xFFFFFFFF while start runs and after a failed start, when it is not known.
interface.scope: No window, no early interrupt, nominal 32kHz oscillator. The reset time is not measured, the reset is not exercised by a build, and a failed start is not recoverable.
interface.state: {{unit}}_state(): 0 not started, 1 running with the reported time, 2 a start failed and the watchdog may be running, 3 start is running (seen only from an interrupt).

pad_capabilities.description: Allocate a digital input on any pad eligible for general allocation. No code is generated: the application initializes the pad as an input with the pull it needs and reads it through the SDK.
pad_capabilities.guidance: Selected GPIO input after mx_system_init: use resource port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api (zero arguments; void). Enable the selected clock, zero hal_gpio_config_t, set mode=HAL_GPIO_MODE_INPUT and pull=HAL_GPIO_PULL_NO, HAL_GPIO_PULL_UP or HAL_GPIO_PULL_DOWN, and check the HAL_GPIO_Init status. Read with HAL_GPIO_ReadPin(port_symbol, pin_symbol), which returns HAL_GPIO_PIN_SET or HAL_GPIO_PIN_RESET. An input without a pull that nothing drives reads an undefined level. Debouncing, thresholds and the external circuit are application matters; for an edge interrupt use gpio_input_interrupt instead. HAL/LL sources are already included and the declarations come from stm32_hal.h; do not redeclare them.
